hypothesis_table.description: The quantified Selmer window stated below. P013 constructs it from a row premise.
The single common nonempty definite-side hypothesis record below. T02 constructs this record under its own inputs.
Green’s parametrization stated below. D575 supplies it from regularity data.
For every real evaluation point, identify the weighted kept host sum with the cyclic-level sum.
A compatible host and its explicit-formula bounds give kept identities, band cardinality, residue-class shares and character derivative bounds.
At a positive explicit-formula scale, bound the discarded nonnegative sum by $4o x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$.
There is an absolute nonnegative constant controlling increments at all points at least one, separately for the principal and nonprincipal characters.
Under the per-unit error windows and the common largeness conditions, bound the local error by the bracket times the indicated exponent loss.
The arithmetic host axioms imply the inertia and Frobenius conditions at the excluded finite set, the auxiliary ramified prime and all other primes.
Fix positive $\varepsilon$ and the constants in the error multiplier. One threshold bounds both the logarithm and that multiplier by $x^\varepsilon$.
Under the finite local host conditions and support cutoff, character orthogonality identifies the difference between the ask and main sums with the deviation.
For every pair of positive widths, the change of the weighted prime sum has absolute value at most three times the scale times the width change divided by the smaller width.
Use the fixed-width thick-place reindexing in th_le. The cited interval and graph size cover its enclosing lemma, which also estimates the error.
For each modulus, exponent and window parameter, obtain good prime pairs with the density and twisted-character prime-sum and zero-free estimates in PairEx.
A primitive character supplies $c,e_0$ before the frame exponent and primes. For each admissible input construct an initial frame and field host, its kernel, twists and conductor bounds.
On the prescribed interval, twist form, conductor divisibility, prime support and PairGood imply pointwise bounds for the complementary frequencies and logarithmic derivatives bounded by $4\log x$.
For each primitive character, frame and raw host, KerChi identifies its field as IsChiField for that same frame exponent and pair of primes.
For every WinPair derive HostHyp, the small odd prime symbols and the two quadratic-reciprocity identities for odd integers.
The size and field conditions, admission, good pair and pair window extend this very initial host to a good host with uniform constants and the required shares.
For each $0<\varepsilon<1/52$ choose the scale threshold before the scale and frame. Order in the required two-sided interval supplies ranks with that exact frame.
For the scale and initial host on that frame, choose ranks with RankVal and admission of the transported host.
Design choices, twisted selection, duty, closed size, class-number estimate and LitThin supply a design on the restricted family class.

Duty, second-layer conditions and mass inputs supply the closed slope/rank and global implications. The surrounding comparison must still supply the slope hypotheses used by the second-layer conditions.
For a family class and absolute constant, division-kernel data above a uniform threshold and closed kernel-constant bounds supply a closed division bound with the very same constant.
A common selection, spectral and base choices, definite height, compatible columns, twists, primitivity, division rows and point data supply the selected wire data.
On one selected family class the remaining comparison inputs supply the closed residual link requirements.
From the closed selected twist estimates with their serving and numerical requirements obtain the family’s linked admissible twists.
The spectral selection, Wu decay, finite rows, frame, counting, local row, mass and selected pretrace inputs supply the closed Bessel/row conclusions.
For any class and twist selection, duty for its members implies a closed eta link on the derived class.
Green and the common joined row/count estimate with positive counting constant yield a closed irreducible-character link.
On the selected derived family class, duty implies the closed G link.
On the given compatible primitive selected data, lambda/division rows and eventual surjectivity of all retained column projections imply the closed small-level rank equalities.
On the compatible selected data, Wu decay, finite rows, the selected realization, base-image fullness and selected-row conditions give a closed comparison of complement forms.
For arbitrary propositions $P,Q,T$ and predicate $N$ on family classes, the shape, proofs of $P,Q$ and one complete HypsAlt witness for $N$ imply $T$.
